Crowley Wins Gubernatorial Election

Exponent, The Exponent | November 5, 2026
image courtesy of The Badger Project
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:54
Instaread

David Crowley has been elected as the 47th governor of Wisconsin, beating Tom Tiffany on Nov. 3.

Crowley entered the race on Sept. 9, 2025. After a middling campaign, he suspended his campaigning efforts on July 8, formerly endorsing Sarah Rodriguez who also later suspended her campaign on July 17. After receiving advice to restart his campaign from current WI Governor Tony Evers, Crowley re-entered the gubernatorial race on July 18, being fully endorsed by Evers the next day.

Despite what the majority of polls claimed, Crowley won the democratic primary, narrowly beating out Francesca Hong by just under 4,000 votes. As part of his victory speech, Crowley said “we rebuilt this campaign with purpose, and after people of Wisconsin decided that the bright future that working Wisconsin families deserve is worth fighting for.”

Crowley then had to run against Tiffany, the Republican Representative. Crowley ran on a platform of “making life more affordable, strengthening our schools, creating good-paying jobs and making sure opportunity reaches every corner of our state.” Crowley has also held the vice chair of the Milwaukee chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union, along with being a member of Milwaukee Urban League Young Professionals, and the Milwaukee National Association for the Advancement of Colored People.

Tiffany announced his campaign on Sept. 25, 2025, and was endorsed by President Donald Trump in January. According to his campaign website, Tiffany “is running for governor to make sure every Wisconsin family has the same shot at the American Dream he was given.”

Crowley and Tiffany both had millions in campaign fundraising, with Crowley getting a total of almost $31 million, and Tiffany getting just over $58 million.

Crowley has served as Milwaukee County executive since May of 2020, and before that served as a member of the 17th district WI State assembly. Crowley will be sworn in on Jan. 4 of next year.
